report:
# Read of unit U1a4 (the-deputy-acts-under-a-recorded-delegation), round 2

Subject: diff against base 4301c698172166a394f99f708132bfc9a65a1ac4, SHA-256 430b09c609fbd20342f44137e1308d74685ea279a7816941eb27da04041aab66 (read.diff and worktree.diff are byte-identical; result.patch has the same hash). Judged against the build brief's AM5 and the 2026-11-14 ruling addendum.

## AGREE

No material findings. Every item AM5 and the addendum ask for is present, correct and tested.

## What was checked

1. Checklist item 1, the diff against the brief:
   - All three sites take the class-dependent limit. The command's parse is `parseGrantEnd(..., classes...)`, called at `intent_grant_everything.go:114` with the classes parsed at `:91`. Creation is `GrantGeneral`, `general_attorney.go:58`, which also re-checks through `WithinBounds` at `:63`. The check of recorded entries is `generalWithinBounds`, `root.go:228`.
   - `GeneralAttorneyLimit` (`root.go:97-104`) gives 30 days only when the grant names classes and every class is in `DelegatedClasses`. Every other grant gets 7 days, including an unclassed one and one naming a retired class.
   - Each refusal names both limits.
   - No other code bounds a general grant's life. `AttorneyMaxDays` belongs to scoped grants and is unchanged. The disposition caller at `intent_decision.go:289` passes no classes and keeps its own refusal text.
   - An old engine that reads a 30-day entry parses it but does not honour it (`WithinBounds` doc, `root.go:137-142`), so the ledger stays readable.
   - The R-152-m1e row is appended as the last row, and no other row changed. It was split into the table's six columns (id, date, ruling, context, owner, review condition). With pipes and spacing removed, its words are identical to the addendum's row (checked by machine).
   - Nothing outside the owner files changed except the one renamed key of an existing test (`general_attorney_test.go:202`), which the reworded refusal required.
2. Checklist item 2, the tests, run by this read:
   - Baseline: `go test ./internal/goal -run 'General|Attorney|Grant'` is ok. `go test ./cmd/metasystem -run 'TestADelegatedOnlyGrantMayRunThirtyDays|TestGrantEndParsesTheEasyForms|GrantEverything|TestIntentGrant'` passes.
   - The engine's round-2 unit check (`check-876797768/output.log`, finished 11:48, after the last edit at 10:40) is green: all of `cmd/metasystem`, `internal/goal`, the other impacted groups and `TestAudit*`, with 0 FAIL.
   - `TestADelegatedOnlyGrantMayRunThirtyDays` is parallel, runs on the injected clock and starts no toolchain.
   - It covers everything AM5 asks for:
     - 720h with `run-release` is recorded and read back by the returned id.
     - On day 29, `work stop run:R` is admitted inside a decision record as `run-release` under that grant, and today's refusal further on is asserted.
     - 744h, and 192h with `run-release,ordering`, are refused at all three sites, and each refusal names both limits.
   - Mutations, run through `go test -overlay` so the worktree stayed untouched:
     - A: 30 days for every general grant. FAIL, because the 192h mixed grant is confirmed.
     - B: creation and parse at 30 days, the recorded check at 7. FAIL, because the 720h add is refused as outside its bounds.
     - C: day 31 instead of day 29. FAIL, because "no live grant admits work stop as run-release". So the injected clock does reach the grant's gate.

## Non-gating observations (fold forward; none is material under R-124)

1. RELATION: new. Help and hint text still promise one week.
   - Where:
     - `cmd/metasystem/intent_planning.go:269`, the `grant add` help: "at most one week".
     - `cmd/metasystem/grant_everything.go:15`, `grantEndExamples`: "a date within the next 7 days".
     - `cmd/metasystem/grant_everything.go:19`, `grantEndOthers`: "--until a date within 7 days". This is the nextReason of the duration refusal itself.
     - The test doc comment at `cmd/metasystem/grant_everything_test.go:20`.
   - Effect: a person reading the help does not learn that a delegated-only grant may run 30 days. A delegated-only grant refused at 31 days gets a next reason that says 7 days, while its summary says 30.
   - Why not material: the refusal summary names both limits and `--for 30d` works. `intent_planning.go` is outside the unit's owner files, so it is OPEN for a follow-up. The two constants are in an owner file.
2. RELATION: new. The reworded refusals dropped concrete values.
   - Creation (`general_attorney.go:59`) no longer gives the latest end ("by ...").
   - The recorded-entry reason (`root.go:229`) no longer names the entry's until and since.
   - Both sites now give one message for two distinct faults: an end before the start, and an end past the limit.
   - "a general grant ends after now: ..." reads as a statement, not a rule.
   - Effect: diagnosing a bad ledger entry is harder.
3. RELATION: new. The limits are written twice.
   - "30 days" and "7 days" are literals in three messages.
   - The 30-day limit is the literal `30 * 24 * time.Hour` (`root.go:101`), with no named constant beside `GeneralAttorneyMax`.
   - Effect: a later change to either limit leaves the messages wrong unless all of them are edited together.
4. RELATION: new. Size against the doubled estimate.
   - Production: 35 changed lines (22 added, 13 deleted) against 30.
   - Tests: 84 against 60.
   - Ruling row: 1, not counted.
   - This is within the 250-line unit bound and fits the known pattern that estimates run double.

## Not checked

Everything on the checklist was checked within the tool budget. This read did not run `devgate static` itself. It relied on the round's green `TestAudit*` run and the green unit check.

VERDICT: land
